description: Uncertainty intervals of task T043. Every count row states one numerator, one denominator, and one confidence level, with the Wilson score bounds one independent implementation of the documented formula computed. Every valid row states one dataset, the evaluated outcomes, and one interval request, with the interval rows the Rust core computes: the case counts of every rate, the draws behind the interval, the bounds, or the reason no bound computes. Every invalid row states the reason code and the field path of its rejection.

metadata.name: Evaluation metric cases
metadata.intended_population: Release notes of one product area. No prevalence claim.
metadata.sampling_method: Selected from reviewed development work. No prevalence claim.

counts.note: One numerator above its own denominator counts one share above its whole.
One fractional count names no case count of one evaluation.
One negative count names no case count of one evaluation.
One count above the dataset record limit names no denominator of one evaluation.
One count stated as text is no number.
No denominator holds no evidence, so no interval computes.

valid.note: One pair for every reference category and every predicted outcome, over eight distinct groups. Every interval counts one case per group, so the independent model applies to every metric of every scope and every slice.

expected.method_statement: Wilson score intervals at 95 percent confidence. Every case of the denominator is one independent draw: no group of the dataset holds two cases of the same denominator. One interval needs its own denominator and at least 1 independent cases. Zero observed errors is not proof of zero risk: the upper bound states the risk the counts still allow.

valid.note: Grouped cases. Three groups hold two cases each, so the group is the draw: the intervals count three groups beside the case counts, and the early slice holds one group alone, below the declared minimum of two.

expected.method_statement: Wilson score intervals at 90 percent confidence. The group is the draw. The interval bounds the share of groups that hold at least one counted event, beside the case counts of the rate. One interval needs its own denominator and at least 2 groups. Zero observed errors is not proof of zero risk: the upper bound states the risk the counts still allow.

valid.note: The declared independent model against one repeated group. thread-1 holds two reference fail cases, so every denominator that holds them both states unsupported_sampling, while the false rejection rate counts reference pass cases alone and keeps one case per group.

expected.method_statement: Wilson score intervals at 99 percent confidence. Every case of the denominator is one independent draw: no group of the dataset holds two cases of the same denominator. One interval needs its own denominator and at least 1 independent cases. Zero observed errors is not proof of zero risk: the upper bound states the risk the counts still allow.

valid.note: An unmet minimum beside zero observed errors. The false acceptance rate counts two cases, below the declared minimum of three, while the false rejection rate of the rule check counts five reference pass cases with no predicted failure and still states one upper bound above zero.

expected.method_statement: Wilson score intervals at 95 percent confidence. Every case of the denominator is one independent draw: no group of the dataset holds two cases of the same denominator. One interval needs its own denominator and at least 3 independent cases. Zero observed errors is not proof of zero risk: the upper bound states the risk the counts still allow.

invalid.note: One confidence level outside the three supported levels.
One confidence level stated as text.
One sampling word the methods support nowhere.
One minimum of zero draws states no evidence requirement.
One fractional minimum names no draw count.
One request without one sampling model declares no assumption.
One request without one confidence level states no level.
One request field outside the request contract.
One request that holds no object states nothing.
